faq.heading: {title} FAQ
faq.q0: Can I see momentum and technical indicators?
faq.a0: Stock analysis uses daily prices to calculate 20- and 60-session price changes and moving averages, 14-session RSI, and volume relative to the previous 20 sessions. Indicators are hidden when price history is insufficient. Live order flow and institutional or foreign investor trades are unavailable.
faq.q1: Can I analyze Korean and U.S. stocks?
faq.a1: Search by Korean stock name or code or by U.S. ticker to see financial metrics and valuations. Available information depends on the market and data coverage.
faq.q2: What methods are used to value stocks?
faq.a2: Compare estimates from models such as NCAV, P/B, S-RIM, DCF, P/E, and PEG. Required financial data varies by stock. Open a model to see its formula and assumptions.
faq.q3: Do the estimates predict future stock prices?
faq.a3: Fair value estimates apply assumptions such as growth rates, discount rates, and multiples to financial data. Estimates change when the inputs or assumptions change.
faq.screenerQ0: Can I combine factors and backtest them?
faq.screenerA0: In the Factor Lab, set ranges, weights, and ranking directions for P/B, P/E, ROE, NCAV, and momentum, then save the combination. To backtest, upload a point-in-time CSV and set the number of holdings, rebalancing interval, and trading costs. Direct access to stored daily scans is limited to admins. The backtest covers the data you provide.
faq.screenerQ1: What does the stock screener show?
faq.screenerA1: Select a strategy such as NCAV, low P/B, low P/E, or S-RIM to see Korean and U.S. stocks that meet its financial criteria.
faq.screenerA2: Net current asset value (NCAV) equals current assets minus total liabilities. The NCAV screen looks for stocks whose NCAV is at least as high as their market capitalization.
faq.screenerQ3: What should I check in the results?
faq.screenerA3: Check the data date and trading status, including suspensions and low liquidity. Open a stock to see its financial metrics and delisting risk signals.

valuation.noData: Financial data is unavailable for fair-value estimates.
valuation.title: Fair value by model
valuation.sameAxis: Shared price scale · Differences are relative to the {reference}
valuation.baseNotice: Differences in the detailed calculations use {price} as the reference.
valuation.noCategory: No estimates are available in this category.
valuation.unavailableEstimate: The inputs were insufficient or the calculated fair value was zero or negative.
valuation.otherDetail: See the model table below for the calculation.
valuation.NCAVDetail: Subtract total liabilities from current assets and divide by shares outstanding. The result is negative if liabilities exceed current assets. Compare estimates by dividing this value by 1.0, 1.2 and 1.5.
valuation.NCAVCaution: Inventory and receivables may realize less cash than their book values.
valuation.PBRDetail: Multiply book value per share (BPS) by 0.6, 1.0 and 1.4 to calculate three price estimates.
valuation.PBRCaution: These multiples are assumptions for comparison and are independent of historical stock prices.
valuation.SRIMDetail: Multiply equity by return on equity (ROE) divided by the required rate of return. The scenarios compare several required returns.
valuation.SRIMCaution: Fair value changes if the current return on equity changes.
valuation.DCFDetail: Apply a constant growth rate to operating cash flow. Discount cash flows for the first five years and the terminal value to the present.
valuation.DCFCaution: The model uses operating cash flow in place of free cash flow. Growth and discount rates materially affect the result.
valuation.PERDetail: Multiply earnings per share (EPS) by preset P/E multiples to estimate several prices.
valuation.PERCaution: One-time gains or losses in the latest annual earnings can affect the estimate.
valuation.PEGDetail: Multiply earnings per share (EPS) by the assumed profit growth rate and the PEG multiple.
valuation.PEGCaution: The model assumes 15% annual earnings growth for all stocks.
valuation.NCAVShort: Examines current assets left after liabilities.
valuation.PBRShort: Compares the share price with net assets per share.
valuation.SRIMShort: Estimates value from return on equity.
valuation.DCFShort: Discounts future cash flows to their present value.
valuation.PERShort: Applies an earnings multiple to earnings per share.
valuation.PEGShort: Estimates value using assumed earnings growth.

financialLabels.costMix: Costs and earnings as a share of revenue
financialLabels.pegFormula: Target price = EPS × earnings growth rate × target PEG
financialLabels.perUsFormula: Fair value = net income / shares × target P/E
financialLabels.krNcav: Market capitalization below or equal to two-thirds of net current assets (about 0.67×) indicates a large asset-based margin of safety.
financialLabels.krSrim: The required return (Ke) is the investor’s minimum acceptable return, typically based on BBB− corporate bond yields. This model uses net income divided by total consolidated equity, including noncontrolling interests. The screener uses EPS divided by BPS, attributable to controlling shareholders. The two can differ considerably for holding companies.
financialLabels.krDcf: Operating cash flow substitutes for free cash flow and is discounted to estimate intrinsic value.
financialLabels.krPer: Compare the current price with estimates based on a range of industry earnings multiples.
financialLabels.krPbr: This model helps assess asset-based downside support for manufacturers and other companies trading at low P/B ratios.
financialLabels.usNcav: This method screens for stocks whose liquidation value substantially exceeds market capitalization.
financialLabels.usSrim: Net income comes from the latest annual filing. The model adds a U.S. bond-market benchmark spread to the required return.
financialLabels.usPeg: Net income comes from the latest annual filing. A PEG below 1.0 indicates a low price relative to assumed earnings growth.
financialLabels.usDcf: Operating cash flow comes from the latest annual filing. This model values the cash-generating ability of large technology and mature companies.
financialLabels.usPer: Net income comes from the latest annual filing. The model helps compare the valuation of technology and consumer stocks.
financialLabels.krAccount0: Assets expected to convert to cash within one year, a key input to NCAV.
financialLabels.krAccount1: Long-term assets such as equipment, land and intangible assets.
financialLabels.krAccount3: Obligations due within one year, used to assess short-term liquidity.
financialLabels.krAccount4: Debts such as borrowings and bonds due in more than one year.
financialLabels.krAccount5: Total obligations. The full amount is deducted from current assets in the NCAV calculation.
financialLabels.krAccount6: The total face value of shares paid in by shareholders.
financialLabels.krAccount7: Earnings retained in the company after dividends.
financialLabels.krAccount8: Assets minus liabilities. This is an input to the S-RIM model.
financialLabels.krAccount9: Total income from sales of products or services.
financialLabels.krAccount10: Direct costs of goods sold, including materials and production.
financialLabels.krAccount12: Selling and administrative expenses, including payroll, marketing and rent.
financialLabels.krAccount13: Gross profit minus selling, general and administrative expenses.
financialLabels.krAccount14: Income from non-operating activities, such as interest and dividends.
financialLabels.krAccount15: Expenses from non-operating activities, such as interest expense.
financialLabels.krAccount16: Operating income adjusted for non-operating gains and losses.
financialLabels.krAccount17: Amounts classified as extraordinary gains in the filing.
financialLabels.krAccount18: Amounts classified as extraordinary losses in the filing.
financialLabels.krAccount19: Ordinary profit plus extraordinary gains minus extraordinary losses. Hidden when the inputs are unavailable.
financialLabels.krAccount20: Calculated pretax income minus net income. It can include other adjustments besides income tax.
financialLabels.krAccount21: Net income after taxes and financing costs.
financialLabels.usAccount0: Cash and highly liquid assets that can be used immediately.
financialLabels.usAccount1: Amounts owed by customers and others. Collection delays can reduce operating cash flow.
financialLabels.usAccount2: Raw materials, work in progress and finished goods.
financialLabels.usAccount3: Assets expected to convert to cash within one year, an input to NCAV.
financialLabels.usAccount5: Total obligations deducted from current assets in NCAV.
financialLabels.usAccount6: Assets minus liabilities, an input to S-RIM.
financialLabels.usAccount7: Total income from sales of products and services.
financialLabels.usAccount8: Income from core operations after costs of revenue and operating expenses.
financialLabels.usAccount9: Pretax results from continuing operations. The scope may differ from final net income.
financialLabels.usAccount10: Reported income tax expense. Negative values are tax benefits. This can differ from taxes paid in cash.
financialLabels.usAccount11: Net income after taxes and financing costs.
financialLabels.usAccount12: Cash generated or used by operating activities.
financialLabels.usAccount13: Cash flows from capital expenditure, asset disposals, and equity investments.
financialLabels.usAccount14: Cash flows from borrowing, repayments, dividends and share buybacks.

risk.usCautionSummary: Potential signs of weakening financial health
